prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a new polished 16:9 pixel-art desktop OS game-screen mockup combining these two references. Reference 1 (older Employee Directory desktop) is the PRIMARY aesthetic, about 80% influence. Reference 2 (olive Mail desktop) supplies only spacious composition, warmth, and readable letter layout, about 20% influence. Preserve reference 1's wonderful chunky deliberate pixel artwork: cream geometric repeating wallpaper, near-black charcoal slightly blue window frame, clearly stepped pixel bevels, warm tan inner borders, cream reading areas, bold readable bitmap fonts, detailed illustrated pixel desktop icons with light boxed labels. This must feel like the old desktop reference, not Windows 95, not a modern dashboard, not ornate fantasy, not a sepia painting. Use bitmap lettering throughout, no serif fonts from reference 2.
Desktop wallpaper: pale cream/tan low-contrast geometric pattern like reference 1. Three big pixel desktop shortcuts down left: 'Mail' with a sealed ivory envelope, 'Directory' with the old brown leather contact-book icon, 'Documents' with a warm ochre folder. No real app logos or Teams logo. One large open Mail window centered slightly right, chunky charcoal titlebar 'Mail' with envelope icon and three pixel beveled window controls like reference 1. Cream folder sidebar with icons and labels 'Inbox (1)', 'Sent', 'Drafts'; Inbox selected in muted amber. Large pale cream main panel with subtle inset tan line border. Exact legible message:
'Welcome to your new office'
'From: Building Manager'
'Nosh,'
'The keys are yours. Make yourself at home.'
'Good luck with the first day.'
Small raised 'Reply' button. Borrow the quiet whitespace and warm cream letter layout of reference 2 while making all lettering and borders authentically pixelated like reference 1.
Bottom full-width chunky charcoal taskbar from reference 1: small generic geometric launcher icon, active Mail tab, inactive Directory tab, tiny sound icon, right side '09:00' and 'Day 01'. Small clearly labeled 'Back to office' button on right of taskbar. No top OS branded banner; NO Warewolf OS, WarewolfOS, or invented OS brand name. No landscape wallpaper. No gold decorative flourishes, character standing in scene, room inventory, quests, RPG meters, graphs, browser chrome, or watermark. Cohesive high-quality game UI mockup with beautifully readable pixel shapes and warm personality.
